bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **TCV down sharply QoQ** — management's "paperwork delay, not demand loss" explanation needs Q3 confirmation (both deals actually signing).
- **Americas-1 decline** (client-specific issues + healthcare softness) — not yet resolved.
- **Health vertical structurally pressured** by US payer policy changes and falling exchange enrollment; recovery only "seasonal, smaller than prior years."
- **Margin-band return (17–17.5%) remains untimed** — contingent on continued AI/business investment.
- **Q3 guide explicitly furlough-driven** — true underlying demand trend for Q3/Q4 not yet visible in the guided range.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Srini Pallia stays consistent on demand ("no change in the demand environment") while being specific and unambiguous that the TCV miss is signing-timing, not lost deals — a claim investors should hold management to in Q3. CFO Aparna Iyer is precise on the margin and other-income bridges, and candid that there is no dated margin-recovery target ("not putting a timeline out there"). Management declines to quantify the Olam/Mindsprint and Alpha-Net inorganic contribution to growth ("not very material"), which limits organic-growth transparency this quarter.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- The **$2.6bn TCV decline is framed entirely as a timing issue** — two large deals whose paperwork slipped into Q3 — rather than a pipeline or demand problem; this is a specific, checkable claim for the next call.
- **Other income fell 68% QoQ** purely mechanically from the completed June-2026 buyback reducing the investable surplus — not an operating signal; EPS (not net income) is the metric management wants tracked post-buyback.
- **No salary hike under consideration** despite a prior hike effective March 2026 — cost base stable into Q3/Q4.
- Health-exchange enrollment data (~18% YoY drop in June) is a leading indicator management declined to size for its book, despite flagging it as context for the vertical's softness.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Consulting-led approach that starts with client business context before technology decisions, differentiating from pure delivery-led competitors
- Wipro Intelligence, a unified suite of AI-powered platforms and solutions (including WINGS and WEGA) underpinning delivery across the portfolio
- Deep industry focus across priority sectors (BFSI, Consumer, Health, Energy/Manufacturing and Resources, Technology and Communications) combined with functional depth (AI advisory, supply chain, finance transformation, people and change, sales/marketing/CX, sustainability)
- Broad global delivery scale: 240,000+ employees and business partners across 65 countries
- Strong enterprise software partner ecosystem (SAP, Oracle, Salesforce, ServiceNow, MS Dynamics) and hyperscaler ecosystem for cloud journeys
- 80-year operating history and 25 years as the first Indian IT services company listed on the NYSE, reflected in long-standing client relationships
- Specialized units (Capco, Aggne, Designit) extending domain depth in banking/capital markets/insurance and design
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body: - Acquisition integration risk — During FY26 Wipro expanded its digital ER&D capabilities through the acquisition of DTS, now operating as Connected Services within Wipro Engineering; integrating a large acquired business into existing engineering practices and delivery structures carries execution risk even as it is intended to deepen AI-powered engineering and R&D capability.

business.body:
- **BFSI (+1% QoQ / +1.3% YoY):** one mega-deal ramp (delayed earlier) now building; a BFSI-Europe client that had insourced work is showing renewed momentum; Capco grew across APMEA, Continental Europe, UK.
- **Americas-1 (−2.1% QoQ):** client-specific issues + healthcare softness.
- **Health (−3.8% QoQ / −6.5% YoY):** US payer/provider budgets under policy-change pressure (incl. ~18% drop in health-exchange enrollments in June); payers tightening discretionary spend, prioritizing AI/automation/compliance; offset partly by first-time outsourcers entering the segment and seasonal Q3 benefit (smaller than prior years).
- **EMR (+1% QoQ / −6% YoY):** prior-quarter wins (CPS, engineering) now ramping; energy segment showing strong traction.
- **Tech & Comms (−2.6% QoQ / +7% YoY):** still YoY-positive; sector continues to compete with BFSI for growth leadership.
- **Consumer (+2.6% QoQ / +6% YoY):** good traction in CPG, travel, transportation; Olam-deal revenue contributing.
- Mindsprint (food/agri, ex-Olam) and HARMAN DTS cited as delivering tangible returns — new logos, deepened engagements — despite near-term margin drag from continued investment.

outlook.title: Strategy

outlook.body: As an asset-light IT services business, Wipro's 'expansion' is footprint, platform and ecosystem build-out rather than physical capacity. It operates 10 innovation/Wipro Innovation Network labs across 10 global locations as of May 2026 (United States, United Kingdom, Australia, UAE, South Korea, and India). Wipro Ventures, its corporate investment arm, has a $500 million fund to invest in early-to-mid-stage enterprise software startups (GenAI/AI, Cybersecurity and Data Security, App Modernization, Data Analytics, DevOps/Test Automation, Vertical SaaS), with 40+ total investments, 25+ companies in the active portfolio, 750+ startup solutions, 280+ global clients over 10 years, and 16 successful portfolio exits. Platform/talent build-out includes Topcoder (an open innovation/crowdsourced talent platform with a global community of over two million developers) and research collaborations with IISc Bengaluru, MIT, and IIT Delhi. During the year the company expanded its AI ecosystem partnerships, including large-scale deployment of Microsoft Copilot Studio, a global collaborative agreement with Factory.ai for agent-native software engineering, an expanded strategic alliance with ServiceNow to embed agentic AI workflows across IT services, HR, procurement and cybersecurity operations, and a strengthened collaboration with OpenAI for AI-led transformation in financial services and energy.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- IT Services segment result margin improved (17.07% to 17.22% of revenue) helped by lower selling & marketing expense ratio, partly offset by higher employee compensation, sub-contracting costs to fill vacant positions, and software license costs from new technology implementation
- IT Products segment revenue growth driven primarily by acquisitions completed during the year and higher revenue from a few select customers in India
- General and administrative expenses as a percentage of revenue rose partly due to the new labor code implementation in India and higher lifetime expected credit loss provisions, partially offset by lower staff recruitment expense and lower average headcount from cost optimization initiatives
- Segment mix shift across Strategic Market Units: Americas 2 revenue share and segment-result contribution rose while Europe's share of revenue and results declined slightly year-on-year
- Sector mix: BFSI remains the largest revenue sector (~34%) with Consumer, Health, Energy/Manufacturing and Resources, and Technology and Communications making up the balance; Technology and Communications share rose while Consumer share declined
- Client concentration: largest client's share of IT Services revenue and top-5 client share both rose year-on-year, indicating increasing reliance on a few large accounts even as the company seeks broader client mining

deepdive.thesis: A flat, in-line quarter — **IT-services revenue $2.61bn (flat QoQ, +0.6% YoY CC)**, margin up 50bps QoQ to 16.5% — masking a **TCV miss** ($2.6bn / 9 large deals, down sharply QoQ) that management attributes purely to **paperwork delay, not demand loss**, with both slipped deals expected to sign in Q3. Wipro Ventures, its corporate investment arm, has a $500 million fund to invest in early-to-mid-stage enterprise software startups (GenAI/AI, Cybersecurity and Data Security, App Modernization, Data Analytics, DevOps/Test Automation, Vertical SaaS), with 40+ total investments, 25+ companies in the active portfolio, 750+ startup solutions, 280+ global clients over 10 years, and 16 successful portfolio exits. Platform/talent build-out includes Topcoder (an open innovation/crowdsourced talent platform with a global community of over two million developers) and research collaborations with IISc Bengaluru, MIT, and IIT Delhi. During the year the company expanded its AI ecosystem partnerships, including large-scale deployment of Microsoft Copilot Studio, a global collaborative agreement with Factory.ai for agent-native software engineering, an expanded strategic alliance with ServiceNow to embed agentic AI workflows across IT services, HR, procurement and cybersecurity operations, and a strengthened collaboration with OpenAI for AI-led transformation in financial services and energy.

themes.title: AI-led IT services & ER&D transformation
themes.need: Q1FY27 split the bucket three ways: a soft large-cap core, a re-accelerating mid-cap tier, and an outright business-model change. TCS grew constant currency only +0.4% QoQ / +3.2% YoY despite $9.5bn of TCV (including an ~$800mn net-new SKF mega-deal), and its AI-services book annualising $2.6bn (+13.6% QoQ) saw incremental adds DECELERATE from +$125mn to +$75mn - AI is still project revenue, not annuity. WIPRO is the laggard (+0.9% YoY cc, margin -120bps to 16.0%, Q2 guided -1.5% to +0.5%). Mid-caps are outgrowing: TECHM grew +6.6% YoY cc with every vertical up and an 11th consecutive quarter of margin expansion (14.4%, +330bps); MPHASIS's pipeline is at an all-time high, 2.8x its size at the Mphasis.ai launch and +28% YoY, with AI-led deals now 70% of it (from 12%) and BFS pipeline +100% YoY, and its new Tria platform closed multiple opportunities within seven weeks of launch; FRACTAL lifted net income +92% YoY on INR 912.5cr revenue at NRR 117% with zero churn (though only +9% cc, dragged by TMT -22%); KPITTECH won $349M of new deals with 21% of pipeline now productized AI/SDV solutions. Structurally, HCLTECH is entering the AI-datacenter business with an initial investment of up to INR 3,500cr and a 50MW long-term ambition, and PERSISTENT is buying Nagarro at EUR 1.27bn EV to build a $2.9bn / 46,000-person group - European scale is now bought, not built. The new cost line is visas: TATAELXSI crossed INR 1,000cr of quarterly revenue for the first time (INR 1,021.1cr) yet EBIT fell 330bps QoQ, with 220-230bps of it onsite/subcontractor investment the CFO said cannot be passed to customers.
themes.driver: MPHASIS's guide that 'Q2 is positioned to deliver the best sequential constant currency growth we have delivered in three years' is the most falsifiable claim in the sector; then HCLTECH's AI-datacenter build, the PERSISTENT-Nagarro close, and whether TCS's AI incremental adds re-accelerate off +$75mn.
